coverage_notes: Prior semantic ledger assesses 1029/1680 cross-module literal name families. The remaining 651 families/1977 clauses are fully indexed with checked source hashes and have disjoint delegated source screens. Tail A leaves 116 local screens and 95 apparent wrappers without full caller tracing; Tail B identifies 84 plausible shared-policy leads requiring reconciliation. The proposals below are selected source-checked findings, not complete name-family coverage or additive LOC savings. The body unit already covers some same-name groups; preserve its IDs on reconciliation.
evidence_artifacts: tooling/name_remaining_index.py (full output in private research root)

findings.title: Issue context text is rendered by three separate helpers
findings.description: All three format `issue_id=<id> issue_identifier=<identifier>`. AgentRunner and State require an Issue struct; AppServer.Messages matches a map. A shared renderer may prevent text drift, but callers retain typed input adaptation and missing-field behavior.
findings.recommendation: Define one issue-context rendering contract near Issue; keep each caller's input validation explicit.

findings.title: Blocker terminal checks repeat across orchestration paths
findings.description: Both clause pairs check a binary blocker state with DispatchPolicy.terminal_issue_state? and use the same terminal set; malformed blockers return false. Sharing the blocker policy does not merge the two dispatch paths or prove blocker evidence is current.
findings.recommendation: Expose a single dependency-state predicate owned by orchestration policy while preserving the false fallback.

findings.title: Pull request topic grammar repeats in poll and webhook normalization
findings.description: The two pr_topic/3 clause sets map opened, ready_for_review and merged to the same ticket topic strings. Their surrounding merge-event recognizers also cover both merged-action and closed-plus-merged shapes. A shared topic constructor should retain source-specific event admission and replay compatibility.
findings.recommendation: Put PR topic construction under an event grammar owner; keep source parsing in each adapter.

findings.title: Membership run ID validation is copied at storage and codec boundaries
findings.description: Both functions require a binary of 1..512 bytes whose trimmed form is unchanged and return the same invalid_run_id error. The codec and path owner need one validation contract so a future format change cannot admit an ID at one boundary that storage rejects at the other. Keeping validation at both ingress points is still appropriate.
findings.recommendation: Use the existing public Store.Paths.valid_run_id/1 or a lower shared membership identity validator from both boundaries, retaining two call sites.

findings.title: Progress percentage normalization repeats across runtime and Stream Deck
findings.description: Both three-clause functions accept integers from zero through 100, round floats, and return nil for unavailable or out-of-range values. The runtime and presentation layers must agree on this measured-value contract. Sharing it should retain nil as unavailable, rather than converting unknown into zero; there is no measured incidence or LOC saving from the source match alone.
findings.recommendation: Own bounded percentage normalization below runtime and presentation adapters, retaining the nil branch and explicit round policy.
